lines.en: Before I knew it, a week had passed since my visit to the Gourmet Association.
And during that week, I had been very busy.
There were now a little over four days left until the ‘Demon King Selection.’
I had to finish all my preparations by then.
Besides the [Black Heavenly Demon Sword] Yoo Joonghyuk had acquired, some quite useful hidden pieces still remained in Murim.
I opened the First Revised Version of ‘Ways of Survival’ and searched through the sub-scenarios where I could collect hidden pieces.
I had read the revised version whenever I had time and skimmed the important parts, but there was still plenty I had missed.
“You've been so busy since you got back. I haven't even had a proper chance to see you.”
Jang Hayoung, wearing an ill-fitting martial arts uniform with oversized sleeves, had been scurrying after me and grumbling for thirty minutes. I frowned, glared at the kid, and asked,
“Aren't you going to train?”
Jang Hayoung pouted and replied,
“······I've been working hard, you know?”
“Working hard, my ass. All I've seen you do is stuff your face with dumplings.”
“Want to try training in seclusion yourself while stuffing your face with nothing but dumplings?”
I was wondering why the kid kept pestering me when something suddenly came to mind.
“Oh, I heard you came third in the tournament? That's a surprise.”
Jang Hayoung's shoulders twitched. Pretending to look elsewhere, the kid said,
“It was no big deal.”
Judging by the way the corners of Jang Hayoung's mouth twitched, the kid seemed pretty pleased.
Now I knew why I'd been followed around so insistently······ What a kid. Couldn't just be honest.
“Did you get your prize? It was a [Demon Spirit Bead], right?”
“Yeah.”
“Let me have it.”
“Why?”
Jang Hayoung backed away with a suspicious look.
I sighed and said,
“I'm not trying to take it from you. You can't eat it as it is anyway.”
From that gloomy expression, it seemed Yoo Joonghyuk had already given the kid an earful too.
I could just picture him drawing the [Black Heavenly Demon Sword] and spouting something like this.
「If you eat it as it is, you'll suffer qi deviation, every acupoint in your body will burst, and you'll die. There is only one person here who can safely absorb that ‘Demon Spirit Bead.’」
······Thinking of it that way, I could understand why Jang Hayoung was so averse to this.
“You don't have to give it to me if you don't want to. You earned it through your own efforts.”
We hadn't built enough trust yet, so I thought there was nothing I could do if Jang Hayoung didn't trust me.
But at that moment, Jang Hayoung suddenly held out a small hand.
“······That's not it. I wouldn't have gotten it without you anyway.”
With a little tap, a small pill dropped into my hand.
This was the [Demon Spirit Bead], one of the three great elixirs of <First Murim>.
I grinned and said,
“Just wait.”
This dark, dingy medicine had a horrific history (前史): the Blood Demon School was said to have made it long ago by refining the souls of as many as 1000 martial masters.

A cursed pill that could open the Ren and Du meridians (任督兩脈) and grant supreme internal power with a single dose, but would turn whoever took it into a madman steeped in demonic qi because of the souls' curse.
Setting aside Yoo Joonghyuk, who had been out of his mind to begin with, Jang Hayoung would certainly die if they took this.
“Let's see······.”

But just as every scenario had its tricks, an item being cursed didn't mean it couldn't be used. In fact, there was a scene in ‘Ways of Survival’ where the Flying Fox absorbed this pill, and I remembered that scene clearly.
「All you need is three Great Return Pills (大還丹). In the end, everything comes down to balance and harmony. If demonic qi is the problem, you just need to supply righteous qi.」
Grinding three [Great Return Pills] together with the [Demon Spirit Bead] and taking them would let you avoid the curse.
Easy to say.
The problem was how on earth to obtain [Great Return Pills], which ranked alongside the [Demon Spirit Bead] as one of the three great elixirs. In truth, though, that wasn't much of a problem for me.
“Biyoo.”
I called Biyoo and opened the [Dokkaebi Bag].
As though it had been waiting, the [Great Return Pill] was already displayed on the [Recommended Products] list.
Those dokkaebis' big data really could be frightening.
[Recommended Products List]
●Great Return Pill ― 200,000 C / Stock: 5
200,000 coins, huh.
Normally, that price would have given me pause. Things were different now.
I deliberately switched the screen to public view before making the purchase.
[You have spent 600,000 coins.]
[You have purchased 3 ‘Great Return Pills.’]
Then channel messages appeared one after another.
[Some constellations envy your extravagant spending.]
[A few constellations are curious about the effects of the Great Return Pill.]
[Several constellations say they will sponsor you with 500 coins if you tell them about the effects of the Great Return Pill.]
“S-Six hundred thousand coins?!”
Han Myungoh, who had been passing by with a dog bowl, was trembling.
He had probably been preparing the Breaking the Sky Sword Master's meal.
“You······ I'd heard you'd become rich, but.”
“Perfect timing. Please take these too and grind them up for me.”
“Wh-What are these? Some kind of elixir?”
“Don't eat them out of curiosity. Take them the wrong way and you'll be cursed by a demon king.”

Han Myungoh went pale at the words ‘cursed by a demon king.’ He took the pills from me and quickly returned after grinding them. The four pills had become a fine powder. I thrust the bowl toward Jang Hayoung.
“I can't take powdered medicine.”
“Put up with it just this once. Hold your nose and swallow it with water.”
“But······ is it really okay for me to take this?”
“It wouldn't do much for me or Yoo Joonghyuk. You're different, though.”

Even without taking the [Demon Spirit Bead], Yoo Joonghyuk would already have a sufficiently developed system for using magic power, and I had the [Broken Heart of a Young Gold Dragon]. Jang Hayoung, however, was probably struggling with a shortage of magic power right now.
Jang Hayoung kept hesitating, so I said,
“If you're not going to take it, give it back. You really have no guts.”
“I'm taking it!”
Jang Hayoung tipped the medicine into their mouth with a slurp and swallowed its bitterness with water.
When Jang Hayoung put down the bowl, the Breaking the Sky Sword Master, who had been lurking nearby waiting for an opportunity, rushed over and enthusiastically licked it.
Checking their condition, Jang Hayoung tilted their head and said,
“······I don't feel anything?”
“The effects will kick in around tomorrow. The pills' energies need time to blend inside your body.”
Jang Hayoung nodded as though they understood.
That was when Han Myungoh, who had been listening beside us, interrupted again.
“Say, Dokja-ssi.”
When I turned toward him, I found a scene I had somewhat expected.
“This car······ did you get it from the ‘Gourmet Association’?”
The ‘car’ he meant was the [X-grade Ferrarghini] sitting unattended in a corner of the estate.
Looking at its sleek black body, capable of crossing even the faults of the Dark Dimension, I suddenly recalled the ‘Mass Production Maker's’ words.
―Don't make too many enemies.
He certainly differed in some ways from the ‘constellations’ I knew.
He would have left an even better impression if he'd given me this car for free.
“Do you think the Gourmet Association is some kind of charity that would give away something like that? I leased it.”
“A lease? H-How much······?”
“Was it 50,000 coins a month?”
“F-Fifty thousand coins? Just how many coins did you earn?”
“About 4.8 million coins.”
At the words ‘4.8 million coins,’ Jang Hayoung and Han Myungoh's jaws dropped at the same time.
Jang Hayoung asked,
“Hey······ aren't you looking for more incarnations?”
“Why, want to be my incarnation?”
When I replied with a chuckle, Jang Hayoung shouted,
“I was just curious! And I've already picked a constellation, you know?”
“A constellation? Who?”
I asked, a little tense.
I wasn't particularly set on taking Jang Hayoung as my incarnation, but things would become complicated if Jang Hayoung chose the wrong constellation sponsor at this point.
But Jang Hayoung said something unexpected.
“The Demon King of Salvation.”
“What?”
“I'm definitely going to be that person's incarnation.”
Seeing the fierce determination burning in Jang Hayoung's eyes, I wondered what kind of joke this was. Thinking it over, though, Jang Hayoung had still never heard my modifier directly.
The kid had been incredibly perceptive in the original······,
No, perhaps the kid simply thought there was no way I could be the ‘Demon King of Salvation’ in the first place.
I suddenly wanted to tease this kid.
“Has that guy even said he'll take you? Have you tried contacting him?”
“Not yet······.”
Seeing Jang Hayoung blush, it seemed the kid really didn't know who I was.
It gave me mixed feelings.
That was when Han Myungoh, who had been watching, interrupted.
“Surely you know his modifier by now?”
“I don't. Do you know, ajusshi?”
Before I could stop him, the oblivious Han Myungoh pointed at me and said,
“He is the ‘Demon King of Salvation.’”
For the next two days, Jang Hayoung avoided me.

The kid, who was usually busy slacking off, suddenly shut himself away in the training hall on the pretext of practicing martial arts and refused to come out. As a result, Yoo Joonghyuk, who had previously had the training hall all to himself, ended up stressed too.
“It seems you've done something pointless again, Kim Dokja.”
“······It's nothing.”

Without much of a reply, Yoo Joonghyuk left the training hall, idly scraping the floor with the [Black Heavenly Demon Sword]. That was something he did when he was in a good mood······ The bastard seemed delighted with his new sword.
The sound of Jang Hayoung pounding a dummy rang out repeatedly from the training hall. It sounded much like me kicking my blankets every night.
“A constellation through and through. It seems you have a taste for peeping.”
When I turned around, an exceptionally tall woman stood there.
Just as I was about to speak, the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint said,
“If you leave off ‘-nim,’ I'll spank you.”
“······Breaking the Sky Sword Saint-nim.”
I couldn't end up like Yoo Joonghyuk over a single syllable.
“Have you been to Tartarus?”
“Not yet. But thanks to you, I've arranged a meeting with the ‘Queen of the Underworld.’”
“I'm glad to hear it.”
Perhaps it was the anticipation of soon meeting her own kind. A fleeting trace of warmth crossed the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's expressionless face.
Gaining her was at least one thing I'd gotten out of this journey.
The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint was a transcendent who ranked among the strongest in all of ‘Ways of Survival.’
With her there, we should somehow be able to get through the ‘Demon King Selection’ too.
“There's something I'm curious about. May I ask?”
“Permission (許) granted.”
“Why did you teach Jang Hayoung martial arts?”
“The kid has talent. Properly honed, it could lead to a new kind of transcendence.”
I knew what she meant.
The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint had probably sensed the ‘wall’ dwelling in Jang Hayoung too.
But that wasn't reason enough.
“You must know that kid is male.”
Originally, [Breaking the Sky Swordsmanship] was a martial art passed down only to women.
Even if Yoo Joonghyuk had somehow been an exception, this martial art, which was not to be taught to outsiders, had never had so many disciples before.
“Still a greenhorn. A Story never has only one interpretation.”
It was a cryptic remark.
Perhaps the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint had realized Jang Hayoung had been a woman in a previous life.
That was when the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint began her story.
“The kid reminded me of a man I once knew.”
“A man?”
“Yes, a man.”
At that moment, I understood perfectly what the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint had meant by ‘A Story never has only one interpretation.’

If the single word ‘man’ could leave me this confused about whether that ‘man’ referred to a lover or simply a male friend······ No, no matter what, there was no way the ‘Breaking the Sky Sword Saint’ could have a lover.
“He was very handsome.”
The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint had never once talked about a ‘man’ in the original, so I began to feel strange.
“You're not going to say Jang Hayoung resembles that ex-lover······ or something, are you?”
I had deliberately said it jokingly, but unexpectedly, the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint answered seriously.
“They do have their good looks in common.”
At this point, I began to suspect she'd accepted Yoo Joonghyuk simply because he was handsome too. But paying no heed to my disappointment, the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint continued.
“Very handsome, but so small that he was rather pitiful.”
For a moment, I wondered whether this was a sophisticated way of mocking her ex-boyfriend. Then a thought suddenly crossed my mind, leaving me aghast.
Someone connected to the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint in ‘Ways of Survival.’
And among those people, the one best described as ‘small.’
No, wait a minute.
Could those two have been on bad terms because······.
Rrrrrumble!
That was when a deafening roar came from outside.
An ominous presence was taking hold of the estate and the surrounding area of Blue Dragon Castle.
The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint and I rushed out of the training hall together. Yoo Joonghyuk looked our way as though he had been waiting.
“Kim Dokja.”
A pitch-black vortex was appearing in the sky.
It was a vortex I knew very well.
A cursed outlet that opened only when a ‘disaster’ appeared in a scenario.
Yoo Joonghyuk gave a low groan and said,
“······[Great Hole].”
‘Disaster scenarios’ normally appeared only in early scenario areas.
There was no way a ‘disaster’ would suddenly appear in <First Murim>.
Disasters didn't appear in scenario areas from the twenties onward.
In areas like those, there was only one reason a ‘Hole’ would open.
A ‘Great Destruction Scenario’ was about to begin in <First Murim>.
In the <Star Stream>, ‘destruction scenarios’ fell broadly into two types.
The first was a Great Destruction Scenario that nebulas had given a name, turning it into a kind of myth (神話). ‘Ragnarok’ and ‘Gigantomachia’ belonged to this category.
The second was a ‘destruction scenario’ that occurred irregularly.
The [Great Hole] that had just opened before us was exactly such a case.
“It isn't a constellation.”
The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's gaze darkened as she looked up at the swirling sky.
If it wasn't a constellation yet exuded that kind of presence, there was only one answer.
“Outer Gods.”
Rrrrrumble―!
Was it because I had become a constellation myself?
I too could vividly feel the power of the gods casting shadows beyond the Hole.
I had certainly encountered parts of those beings several times before.
But what I felt now was on an entirely different level from back then.
A blind person cannot be blinded by looking at the sun.
For the first time, I was on the verge of resenting the fact that I'd become a constellation.
Yoo Joonghyuk muttered,
“······Why has a ‘destruction scenario’ started now, of all times?”
Having already experienced the first and second rounds, Yoo Joonghyuk knew <First Murim>'s future, just as I did.
In the original too, <First Murim> was destroyed by the ‘Outer Gods.’
But this was far too early.
Normally, it wouldn't happen for at least another few years.
Yet something had brought it forward.
What was it? What on earth had gone wrong······?
······Wait, could it be?
Perhaps Yoo Joonghyuk had just had a similar thought, because he asked me,
“······Am I right?”
“I think so.”
I answered tensely.
A ‘destruction scenario’ was a scenario that tested the potential of incarnations.
Unless the required cumulative total was reached through the steady acquisition of probability (蓋然), ‘destruction’ would never begin.
Tzzzzzzzt!
And only one recent event in ‘Blue Dragon Castle’ had triggered that much probability.
The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint said,
“The martial arts tournament?”
The martial arts tournament.
Several constellations, including the ‘Brash Swamp Predator,’ had joined in and supplied probability there. In the end, that had become the catalyst that brought disaster.
[A few constellations who dislike you are delighted.]
Fucking bastards.
“Kim Dokja. Just what did you do there?”
Yoo Joonghyuk, who didn't know exactly what had happened at the Gourmet Association, snapped at me.
I had no excuse to offer.
There was no way to undo a scenario that had already begun.
[The ‘Destruction Scenario’ will begin shortly!]
[An ‘Outer God’ is preparing to attack!]
[Nonparticipants in this scenario are advised to leave the scenario immediately!]
As the messages sounded from the sky, a commotion began in the center of Blue Dragon Castle.
“Fuck! What is that?”
“Run, hurry!”
Unlike other scenarios, a ‘Great Destruction Scenario’ gave you a choice about participating.

Incarnations like us, who wandered from sub-scenario to sub-scenario, were hurriedly leaving the area. The peddlers who sold files containing martial arts formulas, and the martial artists of Blue Dragon Castle who had become masters by listening to those formulas······ The instant the Hole appeared in the sky, all their expressions changed.
Before that ‘Hole,’ the human distinctions between a ‘master’ and a ‘novice’ were utterly meaningless.
“What? What's happening······?”
The startled Jang Hayoung and Han Myungoh belatedly rushed out of the estate too.
“We have to escape, so get ready, quickly.”
Jang Hayoung gasped and pointed at the sky.
There were enormous bundles of tentacles that had broken through the [Great Hole].
It was undoubtedly one of the ‘Outer Gods’ I had encountered in [Peace Land] and [Dark Castle].
【I shall co vet the sto ries of the liv ing】
I shuddered at the terrible presence seeping between its syllables.
At the enormous greed lurking in those words, the fleeing masters wet themselves and collapsed.
“A-Aaaaaaaah!”
An immense chaos that could shatter the minds of living beings with its True Voice alone.
Regardless of how much stronger Yoo Joonghyuk had become, neither he nor I could face something like that now.
Even weak ‘Outer Gods’ possessed the power to trample constellations with ease.
It was also hard to hope for a lucky break through the ‘Fourth Wall,’ as when I had faced the [Eater of Dreams].
[30 minutes remain until the ‘Destruction Scenario’ begins.]
Here, our only choice was to run.
Perhaps this was for the best.
“Breaking the Sky Sword Saint-nim.”
When I looked at the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint, she looked back at me.
Her expression was one I couldn't fully fathom.
「For Namgung Minyoung, the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint, <First Murim> was home.」
All I knew were the sentences written in ‘Ways of Survival.’
And according to those sentences, the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint had no particular reason to protect this place.
「But naturally, not everyone loves their ‘home.’」
To her, <First Murim> was merely a hotbed of the world's corruption.
A world that had lost its humanity and its chivalry.
「“Long before Murim was destroyed, Murim had already been destroyed.”」
The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint had gone so far as to say that. There was no way she would stay here.
<First Murim> would be destroyed like this.
More precisely, it had to be.
“Master.”
Yoo Joonghyuk urged her in a voice that said they should leave at once.
But for some reason, the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint didn't move.

Standing tall as Mount Tai, the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint simply stood in silence, looking across the narrow road. A city plunged into chaos by riots and flight. And a group of people approaching through that scene.
Masters who were each already on the verge of transcendence or had attained it.
The moment I sensed the brilliant energy surrounding their bodies, I realized who they were.
“Breaking the Sky Sword Saint, it has been a long time.”
The heads of Blue Dragon Castle's great families (勢家主) had come to see the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint.
It wasn't hard to guess why they had come.
The ‘Outer Gods’ had come to Murim, and destruction was set to follow.
Faced with destruction, Murim's martial artists responded in one of two ways.
Flee, or stand and fight.

Those with little to lose would choose the former, but incarnations who had stayed and put down roots here over many years were different. Building influence, amassing wealth, creating Stories. Those who had at last reached the pinnacle of power in a region.
“Breaking the Sky Sword Saint. We need your help.”
From left to right, the Zhuge Family, the Murong Family, the Sichuan Tangmen School, the Hwangbo Family, and finally the Namgung Family.
For the heads of all five powers that formed the backbone of <First Murim> to gather here was probably rare even in the whole of Murim's history.
The leaders of major sects were among those standing behind them too.
“We beg you. Lend us your strength for Murim.”
Namgung Minyoung quietly clenched and unclenched her fist as she answered.
“You need my strength······.”
At that icy voice, several of the family heads flinched and stepped back.
The first to step forward was the quick-witted head of the Zhuge Family.
“Please help us. We humbly beg you.”
I could understand why they were behaving this way.
The Ice Flower Goddess, who had claimed to be Murim's greatest living master, had been defeated by a mere ‘disciple’ of the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint, rather than the Sword Saint herself.
With an overwhelming disparity in their abilities, at that.
The shock of the martial arts tournament had probably served as a warning to countless masters who had taken only the easy path.
Power capable of defeating even a descended constellation.
The masters had grown nostalgic for the old path of transcendence once more, and when crisis came to Murim, they recalled the person who had reached that path's pinnacle.
“Great martial elder, please look kindly upon the younger generations.”
Finally, even the head of the Namgung Family, the birth family of Namgung Minyoung, the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint, joined in.
A middle-aged person with a dignified face.
That was probably Namgung Jincheon, one of the Ten Great Masters.
Even if it was only half, the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint had that family's blood in her veins.
Perhaps that was why even her proud gaze wavered for a moment.
Unable to watch any longer, I stepped forward.
“How ridiculous. Weren't you the ones who cast out the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint-nim first?”
Normally, I wouldn't have done anything to provoke their collective anger.
I would instead have considered how to bring them along to the ‘Demon King Selection.’
But securing the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint was more urgent now.
“Pathetically enough, you seem to have forgotten everything you did when constellations and dokkaebis first visited this place.”
“What······ Who are you?”
Several family heads realized what I meant, and their expressions changed abruptly.
They probably remembered too.
Why the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint, who had reigned at the pinnacle of Murim, had ended up running an estate on a run-down side street.
Only Yoo Joonghyuk, who knew the whole story, quietly bit his lip at my words.
Namgung Minyoung, the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint, was a warped, obstinate woman, but she understood chivalry (俠).
Not swept along by the tides of the world, she did not blame others.
Not pursuing honor, she did not covet the hollow fortunes of glory and disgrace.
And so she had spent her life being exploited by Murim's martial artists, only to be abandoned here in the end.
Leaving the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint as a symbol of fallen Murim, the family heads had built their own castles and taken control of Murim.
“Head of the Namgung Family, you're no different. ‘Great martial elder’······ You've never once called the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint that before, have you?”
“If you had any sense at all, you wouldn't have come here. I can't tell whether you're brave or stupid. Surely you know why the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint broke ties with your Namgung Family?”
A child born of mixed giant and human blood.
I knew the ordeals the young Breaking the Sky Sword Saint had endured growing up better than anyone in this world—perhaps even better than Yoo Joonghyuk.
「How could a girl······!」
「She carries the cursed blood of the giants.」
The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint looked puzzled.
She would be wondering how I knew those things.
Normally, these would have been dangerous things to say, but her questions were actually to my advantage now. The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint would follow me, if only to have them answered.
“What do you know, you bastard······!”
“Shut your mouth! Breaking the Sky Sword Saint, who on earth is that man!”
As the agitated family heads approached, threatening me, Yoo Joonghyuk drew the [Black Heavenly Demon Sword].
This was actually for the best.
If a clash broke out here, we could use it as a pretext to leave without trouble.
But before the furious Yoo Joonghyuk could shout at them, the head of the Zhuge Family suddenly prostrated themselves on the ground.
“Breaking the Sky Sword Saint, we regret our past wrongs. We also know well that we cannot undo them.”
······Damn it, every world had clever bastards like this.
The Zhuge Family head's sudden action left the other family heads flustered.
Casting aside all dignity and decorum, the head of the Zhuge Family pleaded earnestly with the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint.
As though praying to the god (神) of Murim.
“If you don't help us, <First Murim> will be destroyed······!”
It was the gaze of a believer who could demand a god's compassion whenever they wished, yet was ready to abandon that faith at any moment.
Then the god of Murim answered.
“Once, small trees gathered to form a forest.”
At those unexpected words, the head of the Zhuge Family raised their head to look at the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint.
“But now all the small trees have been uprooted, and only a few great trees that seized their ground spread their branches to cover the sky.”
With an expressionless gaze, the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint looked over Blue Dragon Castle.
The great families' spires, rising as though in competition, pierced the sky high above the battlements.
As though they would watch over them in heaven's stead.
Only then did I understand the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's words.
“Their leaves and branches may be lush, but now there are only a few trees. What do you think? Can that still be called a ‘forest’?”
Murim (武林), the martial forest, had died long ago.
That was what the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint had just declared.
“Let us go now.”
The god of Murim quietly turned her back and forsook the world.

Things seemed to be going more easily than expected, so I followed the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint, satisfied. Yoo Joonghyuk, who had been staring blankly at me, and Jang Hayoung and Han Myungoh, who had been packing dumplings behind us, quickly gathered their belongings too.
But at that moment, I heard a strange message.
[Your actions have profoundly influenced the course of ■■.]
[The ‘Second Revised Version’ update will begin.]
[Author's Note]
Hello, readers.
Today, I would like to make an important announcement about the future publication schedule.
I began thinking about this around the time my health, which had steadily worsened since shortly after the paid serialization began, started sending warning signals.

Spending all day typing away at the keyboard without even time to go to the hospital, I found more and more parts of my body hurting, one after another. Even so, I wanted to keep my promise to you, the readers. Just until episode 150, just until episode 200... With those thoughts, I somehow held on. And finally, episode 250... When I woke in the middle of the night in severe pain, a thought suddenly struck me.
Ah, if I keep going like this, this novel will never reach its ending.
Starting with episode 250, Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint will change its publication schedule to five installments a week.

There are the hospital appointments I made but never managed to attend... but in truth, I also made this decision to improve the quality of the writing. Since Kim Dokja's story is now getting fully underway and the level of engagement is increasing... To the readers who have followed me this far, to cause disappointment
The Second Revised Version update.
Hearing that message at an unexpected moment, my mind suddenly filled with thoughts.
Another revised version meant my actions were continuing to alter the future.
In other words, all the narratives I had built since receiving the First Revised Version had once again come together and contributed to creating a new future.
At that thought, my heart began to race.
Had my third-round self succeeded?
Would I be absent from the fourth round again this time?
Had Yoo Joonghyuk reached the ending through the story I had changed?
······Why on earth did the author keep sending me things like this?
[The ‘Second Revised Version’ update is in progress.]

The file hadn't been updated yet, so I couldn't be certain of anything. I didn't know whether things had become worse or better. In fact, what I needed to think about now wasn't where the new revised version would lead, but the unfolding events right before my eyes.
“Breaking the Sky Sword Saint! Are you running away now? Are you going to abandon this entire world you've lived in and flee?”
While I had been briefly distracted by ‘Ways of Survival,’ the masters had all risen to their feet. The loudest denunciation came from the head of the Zhuge Family, who had been the first to kneel.
“······Running away? Me?”
“What else would you call what you're doing now!”
“How amusing, children.”
Her voice was thick with derision. In response, the martial artists all gave battle cries and unleashed their auras.
Whoooooom!
Every one of them was a renowned master in <First Murim>. With the family heads' magic power added to theirs, menacing seismic waves began surging through the estate's surroundings.
Facing the family heads as they raised their auras, the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint stamped her foot.
Boooom!
“Khuuugh!”

It was an unbelievable sight. The shock wave spreading from the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's stamping foot precisely canceled out the seismic waves they had unleashed, then inflicted internal injuries on every master with magic power several times greater than theirs.
All of it had happened with one simple stamp of her foot.
This was the power of the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint, known as the disaster of <First Murim>.
The masters collapsed, spraying blood, and looked up at the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint with resentful eyes.
“B-Breaking the Sky Sword Saint!”
“Don't abandon us! Please!”
Did they believe that power like this could surely stop ‘destruction’?
The martial artists coughing up blood showed traces of hope rather than despair.
As the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint looked down at them with an expressionless gaze, the [Great Hole] in the sky was growing larger and larger.

Until now.

10 seconds.

Hidden Scenario ― ‘Kim Dokja Proof of Identity.’

The Immortal Doctor, Lee Seolhwa.
A former companion of Yoo Joonghyuk, she was caring for patients here.

In the end, both of them with only uncertain information about the future.

Lee Sookyung smiled at the two of them.

―Great misfortune (大凶).

助, the character jo, meaning ‘to help.’
